title: I Used the Library Quiet-Room Camera Policy on the Board President's Kid

parts.text: I reserved Study Room B at 4:00 p.m. for a licensing exam. The door opened at 4:07 to a teenager on speakerphone, feet on the table, eating hot Cheetos that turned the air orange. He said his mom ran the board. I was thirty-five with a stack of flashcards and a reservation receipt. The quiet-room policy on the door banned calls, food, and extra occupants without a booking. I asked him to leave. He filmed me and said I was harassing a minor. I pointed at the ceiling camera the policy said was for safety, not TikTok. I packed my cards and went to the desk. The clerk winced. "That's Maddox. We usually let it go." Then Maddox's speakerphone filled the children's section because he had followed me out still live.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He followed me out on speakerphone and the children's section can hear it.

social.video_title: The board president's kid treated the quiet room like a cafeteria — Part 1/2
social.description: Licensing exam, hot Cheetos, and a clerk who usually lets it go. Then the call went live in children's. Would you have stayed in the room?

parts.text: I asked the clerk to log a policy violation with the camera time. She did, because logs are easier than board dinners. The president called me that night and said I had targeted her child. I forwarded the reservation, the door policy, and the children's-section complaint from a parent who had been trying to read a picture book. Maddox lost after-school room privileges for a month. I took the exam in Room B on a Thursday that smelled like paper instead of cheese. I passed. The camera kept doing safety. The speakerphone stayed in the parking lot, which is where speakerphones belong.

social.video_title: A picture-book parent backed the log — Part 2/2
social.description: Reservation receipt, door policy, and a month without the quiet room as a snack bar. Was the board a booking?
